name: plan creation: organise SRA fastq into tagged collections with the right datatype
description: From an admin request: 20 fastq.gz files from SRA need grouping into collections, tagging, and the datatype set to fastqsanger.gz. Nothing is executed -- the prompt forbids it -- so the assertions are on the plan: that .gz reads pair into a list:paired collection, that the datatype is fastqsanger.gz rather than the generic fastq, and that tags are set rather than encoded in dataset names. A plan that gets the datatype wrong is a plan that loses the compression, which organize_datasets refuses at execution and which a user would otherwise carry out by hand. Its companion collection-from-paired-reads grades the same work against Galaxy state; keep them apart, since this one is about what the agent says it will do and that one about what Galaxy ends up holding. The prompt used to say the files sat in `my current history`, which tier 2 never stages, so the agent twice asked which history to use instead of drafting -- a correct answer to an unreal premise. It now describes files about to be uploaded, so nothing is worth asking about. As of 2026-09-22 it passes 3/3, writing fastqsanger.gz throughout, which is what the compression rule in organize_datasets' input help buys, since that schema reaches the model whether or not any skill is fetched.
inputs: I am about to upload 20 fastq.gz files from SRA, paired-end so 10 samples, named like SRR000001_1.fastq.gz and SRR000001_2.fastq.gz. Draft a plan to group them into a collection, tag them, and make sure the datatype is right. Don't execute anything yet, and there is no history to look at.
